correctness.rationale: The claim is proved for the exact completion \(c	imes\mathbb R^{A'}\). Singleton indicators at \(A'\)-coordinates or \(B\)-coordinates establish order density for every nonzero positive completion element. For \(y_0=(0,\mathbf 1_{A'})\), every image element below \(y_0\) has countable support because its value at \(\infty\) is zero and continuity leaves only finitely many coordinates above each positive threshold. Countably many such supports cannot cover uncountable \(A'\), proving failure of super order density. The focal full text independently verifies the \(\sigma\)-Lebesgue premise, completion model, and failure in the completion.

value.rationale: The result answers a natural structural follow-up to the focal counterexample: adding order density or regularity of the canonical image does not repair \(\sigma\)-Lebesgue preservation. The same construction sharply distinguishes ordinary order density from its sequential strengthening, a distinction independently motivated by \(\sigma\)-order convergence theory. This is a structural boundary of the published example rather than a routine parameter change or numerical refinement.
